violations.why: req6 (higher priority than req1) can set irq=-1 between req1's write of irq and its check, so the irq==0 test can fail.
req7 (higher priority) can set irq=0 between req6's write of -1 and its check of irq==-1.
req3 sets global_id=-1 in exit and then tests it. A higher-priority ISR (req5, req7) can run init in between and overwrite it.
A higher-priority ISR's exit can overwrite global_id between req3's init write and its read at 331.
req3 (higher priority) can write var1 between the two reads in JudgeCondi, which runs in req1. The two reads can then see different values.
req3 can write var2 between the two reads in JudgeCondi, which runs in req1.
req8 (higher priority than req7) writes array[9000] between req7's write and its read.
